queue.key_answer:
Dear Tom,
I am sorry to hear that you are under great pressure and can't sleep well at night. Here are some suggestions that may help you.
First, you should plan your time carefully and avoid leaving tasks until the last minute. Second, doing some exercise for half an hour before bed, such as jogging or stretching, can help you relax. Third, try not to use screens an hour before sleep; reading a book instead may help you fall asleep more easily.
I hope these suggestions will be useful to you. Best wishes!
Yours,
Li Hua
queue.proposed:
Dear Tom,

I'm sorry to hear that you have been under a lot of stress and sleeping badly. Here are a few suggestions. First, make a proper study plan and balance work with rest. Second, take exercise regularly, such as walking or running, which helps you sleep better. Third, stay away from your phone before bedtime; listening to soft music works well. Besides, sharing your worries with friends or family can also help.

I hope you will feel better soon.

Yours,
Li Hua

queue.key_answer:
Dear David,
I'm glad to know you are interested in the Spring Festival, the most important traditional festival in China. It falls on the first day of the lunar calendar.

Before the festival, people put up Spring Festival couplets on doors and set off fireworks to welcome the new year. On New Year's Eve, the whole family gathers together for a big dinner, which is called "Nian Ye Fan". Children receive red packets with lucky money inside, which bring them good wishes.

I sincerely invite you to come to my hometown and spend the Spring Festival with my family. I'm sure you will have an unforgettable experience.

Yours,
Li Hua
queue.proposed:
Dear David,

I'm glad that you want to know about the Spring Festival, the most important traditional festival in China. Before it comes, people clean their houses and put up red couplets. On New Year's Eve, families get together to enjoy a big dinner, and children usually receive red packets from their elders. During the festival, people visit relatives and friends, and beautiful fireworks light up the sky.

Come to China and spend the Spring Festival with my family! You will surely have a wonderful time.

Yours,
Li Hua

queue.key_answer:
Good afternoon, everyone!
My topic today is "Persistence and Dreams". I believe a clear dream gives us direction, while persistence turns the dream into reality. Without hard work, even the brightest dream will only remain an idea.
Here are my suggestions. First, set a clear and realistic goal for yourself. Second, break the big goal into small steps and celebrate each small success. Third, never give up when you face difficulties; remember that every failure is a step closer to success.
Let's hold on to our dreams and keep moving forward. Thank you!
queue.proposed:
Dear friends,

It is a great honor to speak on the topic Persistence and Dreams. Everyone has dreams, but dreams alone are not enough. Only with persistence can we turn them into reality. First, break your dream into small goals and work on them every day. Second, never give up when you fail, because every failure teaches you a lesson. Third, keep a positive attitude and believe in yourself.

Where there is a will, there is a way. Let's hold on to our dreams and keep moving forward!

He told the boy that he used to be a teacher, but now he had lost his job and his home, and he had not eaten anything for two whole days. "You are the kindest person I have ever met," he said in a trembling voice. Tom felt both sad and proud. The cold wind seemed less bitter, and the two shared a moment of warmth on the cold street.

Then she hugged him tightly and said with tears in her eyes, "My dear, the best present you can give me is to grow into a kind and generous person like this." He was a retired worker; his son worked far away, and he had lost his wallet on his way home, so he had not eaten for a whole day. Tom listened quietly and felt something tighten in his chest. Don't worry, sir. I'll come back with some food, Tom said. The old man held the five dollars tightly, thanking him again and again. Tom waved goodbye and ran towards home, feeling strangely warm inside even in the cold wind.

Paragraph 2: When Tom arrived home and told his mother what he had done, she had a special reaction: she smiled and said, You did the right thing. Hearing this, Tom felt relieved. His mother then prepared a bowl of hot noodles and a clean blanket, and together they walked back to the old man. The old man's eyes filled with tears when he saw them. On the way home, Tom held his mother's hand tightly, knowing that the warmth in his heart mattered far more than any present.

Paragraph 1: As the race began, Lin pushed himself forward, but halfway through he felt dizzy and his legs grew heavy. He almost fell, but the cheers of his schoolmates encouraged him to keep going. However, on the last lap, his cold got worse and he had to slow down. Although he tried his best, he finished only fifth, far below his usual position. He felt both disappointed and physically exhausted when he crossed the finish line.

Paragraph 2: When Lin returned to school with his head down, his coach walked up to him with a warm smile and said, "Lin, you have already won the most important race of all — the race against yourself." At that moment, Lin realised that true courage is not about winning but about never giving up. From that day on, he became more confident in everything he did.
queue.proposed:
Paragraph 1: The race began, and something unexpected happened to Lin. He started well, but after 200 metres his head began to spin. Suddenly he stumbled and fell! Pain shot through his knee, and the other runners rushed past him. For a moment he wanted to stay on the ground. Then his coach's words echoed in his mind: Never give up. Gritting his teeth, Lin got to his feet and moved forward step by step. When the crowd saw him running again, the whole stadium stood up and cheered for him.

Paragraph 2: Although the result was not what he had hoped for, Lin learned something important from the race. He finished last, but as he crossed the finishing line, his teammates lifted him onto their shoulders. The coach told him that his courage was the real victory. On the way home, Lin smiled despite his painful knee. He understood that life is not always about winning; what truly matters is having the courage to finish the race you have started.
